scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: Kir2.1 can plausibly increase resting potassium conductance and thereby lower input resistance. However, the broad assignment of high Kcnj2 to Pvalb cells and low Kcnj2 to Vip and Sst cells is insufficiently established and likely oversimplifies subtype-specific conductance differences.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: The response explicitly connects Kcnj2 expression to Kir2.1 conductance, current shunting, and lower input resistance, while using Pvalb, Vip, and Sst identities to define contrasting expression states. It does not explain what produces the proposed cell-type-specific Kcnj2 regulation, and morphology remains an acknowledged but disconnected alternative determinant. No synthesis ceiling was applied because an explicit and biologically reasonable focus-feature–target mechanism was provided.
